project.name: blogagent-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the blog generation agent (V9 §18 / §91).
Members. BlogAgentPort (5 methods) with three narrowed records (BlogAgentTaskDraft, BlogAgentTaskView, BlogAgentPostView); plus BlogAgentImagePort (2 methods) with BlogAgentImage (6 components) and BlogAgentImageUsage (3 longs). Two rounds, one module: the second round extends the first with zero build wiring.
Why the module exists. Four statements in three files reached into blogagent's application layer, and two more reached into its api layer:
agent -> blogagent (4 impl / 2 api) BlogGenerationTool, PublishPostTool, ImageGenerationTool agent -> publishing (0 impl / 1 api) PublishPostTool
BlogGenerationTool and PublishPostTool imported blogagent.application.BlogAgentService together with blogagent.api.*, and PublishPostTool additionally imported publishing.api.BlogPostVO, because that is what BlogAgentService.publish returns. ImageGenerationTool reached past the service into blogagent.infrastructure. After the split dinqor-agent could not be built without blogagent's implementation classes AND without publishing's api layer.
What this cut takes. Both capabilities. Round one took the service capability (the two tools that go through BlogAgentService) and cleared agent -> publishing outright (PublishPostTool was the only cross-domain reader of BlogPostVO), shortening agent -> blogagent from 4 to 2. Round two took the image capability, which zeroes agent -> blogagent: the edge is gone.
Why the image capability is a SECOND port, not a method on BlogAgentPort. Because the shape is different. BlogAgentImagePort's provider is a concrete client (BlogAgentImageClient: RestClient + HttpClient + endpoint fallback) plus a @ConfigurationProperties bean, not a domain method on a user-owned resource. It is also the one port that takes no userId, deliberately: the provider is a stateless model call, and the two steps that do need identity (saving the asset, charging points) are on MediaAssetPort and BillingPort, both of which take userId explicitly. A guard asserts NO parameter here is named userId, so nobody "restores consistency" by adding one that nothing reads.
The image capability's own two shape decisions. The generated image travels as bytes (byte[]), which MediaAssetPort.recordGenerated already does, so the precedent exists. The token usage travels as a three-long record, because ModelUsage lives in libs/xander-model, which declares jackson-databind for ModelUsage.fromJson; a contract may not depend on a library that drags in Jackson (ADR-1). Hence BlogAgentImageUsage, which is deliberately shape-identical to payment.api.TokenUsage and deliberately written twice: a contract may not depend on a contract.
Why BlogAgentImage carries model and size. Because the alternative is worse. If the port returned only the bytes, the consumer would have to read blog.agent's @ConfigurationProperties itself, which turns the provider's configuration into a cross-domain contract -- and configuration is free to be renamed, defaulted or absent (it is absent on the gateway path). So the provider's adapter fills in what this generation actually used. Note model comes from the generated result, NOT from properties.getImageModel(): the client retries across candidate endpoints, so the model that produced the image may be the fallback one, and on the gateway path the configured model may be blank. Recording the configured value instead was a live bug in ImageGenerationTool, fixed by this cut; BlogAgentService already recorded the actual model on the same-domain illustration path.
Why the DTOs are NARROWED, not mirrored. The mirror rule (ADR §2.5) exists for a type that *replaces* a frontend-visible one: mirroring then makes "serialization is byte-identical" provable, which is what keeps the cut a pure refactor. Nothing here replaces anything. blogagent.api.BlogAgentTaskVO stays exactly where it is and keeps going to the frontend unchanged from blogagent.api.BlogAgentController; so does publishing.api.BlogPostVO. Every type in this module is new, on a new seam the frontend never sees, so each carries exactly the components its consumers read:
BlogAgentTaskView 4 of the domain entity's 25 id, title, summary, publishedPostId BlogAgentPostView 5 of BlogPostVO's 17 id, title, status, csdnSynced, juejinSynced BlogAgentTaskDraft mirrors BlogAgentTaskCreateRequest's 2 fields, without @NotBlank BlogAgentImage 6 bytes, contentType, extension, usage, model, size (the first five line up positionally with the provider's GeneratedImage; size is appended at the END on purpose, so "positional" stays true)
What IS pinned is the component order, by reflection, and the mapping entity/VO -> record, by an app-module test using mutually distinct literals.
Why jakarta.validation annotations are NOT here. blogagent.api.BlogAgentTaskCreateRequest carries @NotBlank and @Size, and those fire only because BlogAgentController annotates the parameter @Valid. A contract may not carry them anyway (they would add a dependency, and ADR-1 keeps this module framework-free). Nothing is lost on the agent path, which never had them: the tools build their arguments from JSON, and BlogAgentService validates the fields itself in normalizeClientRequestId. BlogAgentTaskDraft mirrors the request's two fields without the annotations, and the domain-side request type stays the validated front door for the HTTP callers.
Why every method of BlogAgentPort takes the caller id FIRST, and why BlogAgentImagePort is the one exception. All four earlier contracts put userId first, and the guard test that pins it asserts the first parameter's TYPE is Long -- which is a weaker statement than the invariant it is named for. Four of the five methods BlogAgentPort wraps declare their parameters the other way round on the provider side (publish(taskId, userId), findPublishedPost(taskId, userId), runStream(taskId, userId, ...)), so mirroring the provider's order would have made the port inconsistent while still passing that guard. Instead the port normalises to (userId, ...) and the provider's thin adapters swap explicitly, one line each, pinned by a mapping test whose two literals differ (42 vs 9). BlogAgentPortTest asserts the first parameter is NAMED userId, not merely typed Long -- javac is run with -parameters here, so the name survives into the class file, and that closes the gap between what the guard says and what it checks.
BlogAgentImagePort takes no userId at all, and that is a decision rather than an oversight (see above). Its guard is therefore the REVERSE one: it asserts that no parameter anywhere in that port is named userId. Without that, "consistency" would creep back in as an unused parameter, and the next reader would go looking for where it is used.
Package note: this module's package is com.xander.lab.blogagent.spi, NOT com.xander.lab.blogagent.api. blogagent already owns com.xander.lab.blogagent.api as its *frontend HTTP* layer (BlogAgentController, BlogAgentTaskCreateRequest, BlogAgentTaskVO, BlogAgentSessionVO, BlogAgentMessageRequest). Declaring the contract there would put one package in two jars, and would make the scanner classify those controllers as shared kernel, turning "a controller imports its own application layer" into dozens of blogagent.api -> blogagent backlog edges plus a shared-kernel-reverse-dependency violation each. Same collision as agent-api, automation-api, recitation-api and studio-api; same answer. SHARED_KERNEL lists blogagent.spi (dotted, matched longest-first, so it does not swallow blogagent.application, blogagent.domain or blogagent.infrastructure).
What is deliberately NOT here yet: - generateTopicSeries, whose only caller is automation.BlogContentPlanService -- same deployment unit (both are dinqor-content-automation), so converting it would move no cross-unit metric. It is a candidate for a later tidy-up, not for this cut. - listSessions / reviseStream / reviewCompliance / findTaskByClientRequestId: their callers are BlogAgentController and BlogAgentService's own pipeline. - blogagent's own same-domain illustration path (BlogAgentService.illustrate), which keeps using BlogAgentImageClient directly. The port serves cross-domain consumers only; that is also why GeneratedImage needed no change at all -- the port's adapter converts, the same-domain path is untouched. - Any of blogagent's own api layer (com.xander.lab.blogagent.api.*). It is the frontend HTTP contract, a different audience, and it joins a contract module only when that layer itself is split in Wave 2.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
